reasoning: The problem (verbosity/length bias in reward models) is heavily studied and the specific contribution—measuring how universal and strong length bias is across a panel of open reward models—is already directly addressed. "One Bias After Another" (arXiv 2603.03291, 2026) systematically measures length bias across five high-quality RMs, and "Post-hoc Reward Calibration: A Case Study on Length Bias" (arXiv 2409.17407, ICLR 2025) estimates per-model length bias across 33 RewardBench-leaderboard reward models. The proposed matched-content/vary-only-length pair methodology with preference-flip counting is also established: reWordBench (EMNLP 2025) uses meaning/ranking-preserving input transformations, RewardBench itself includes length-controlled subsets, and several works construct "length-divergent, content-matched response pairs" and report a Preference-Flip Ratio / Win-Rate-by-Length-Difference. Remaining gaps are minor: an explicit comparative "verbosity susceptibility leaderboard" with confidence intervals as the headline deliverable, and the filler-vs-restatement padding-style ablation, are not isolated as a standalone contribution in any single paper—but the methods and cross-model measurements exist across multiple published works, so the contribution would be largely a repackaging/replication.

evidence.title: One Bias After Another: Mechanistic Reward Shaping and Persistent Biases in Language Reward Models
evidence.summary: Systematically measures biases in five high-quality reward models, finding persistent length bias (plus sycophancy, overconfidence, style, answer-order). Directly answers the proposal's cross-model question of how universal/strong length bias is, in a controlled setting.

evidence.title: Post-hoc Reward Calibration: A Case Study on Length Bias
evidence.summary: Estimates and removes a length-bias term across 33 Bradley-Terry reward models from the RewardBench leaderboard. Provides exactly the multi-open-model, comparative length-bias quantification the proposal aims to produce.

evidence.title: reWordBench: Benchmarking and Improving the Robustness of Reward Models with Transformed Inputs
evidence.summary: Benchmarks reward models under meaning/ranking-preserving input transformations (inference-only), the same paradigm as padding content-matched pairs to isolate spurious cues; finds SOTA RMs degrade sharply, sometimes below random.

evidence.title: RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models for Language Modeling
evidence.summary: The reward-model evaluation suite the proposal draws its model panel from; already includes length-controlled subsets and analyses of bias against spurious cues such as length/token frequency across many open RMs.

evidence.title: Flattery, Fluff, and Fog: Diagnosing and Mitigating Idiosyncratic Biases in Preference Models
evidence.summary: Diagnoses idiosyncratic biases including fluff/verbosity across preference (reward) models, overlapping with the proposal's filler-padding susceptibility angle.

evidence.title: Disentangling Length Bias in Preference Learning via Response-Conditioned Modeling
evidence.summary: Uses length-divergent content-matched and length-matched content-divergent response pairs to isolate length from content, the exact matched-pair construction the proposal describes.
